events.title: Gutenberg Bible Printing Reaches Public Notice
events.description: On or around this date, the Gutenberg Bible, the first major book printed with movable metal type in Europe, is commonly dated by some references to have been completed or circulated by the mid-1450s; March 22, 1457 is more reliably associated with the Mainz Psalter's printing era under Fust and Schöffer.
events.significance: The spread of movable-type printing transformed the production of knowledge, enabling the Renaissance, Reformation and the rise of mass literacy.

events.title: British Parliament Passes the Stamp Act
events.description: Parliament passed the Stamp Act, imposing a direct tax on printed materials and legal documents in the American colonies to help pay for British troops stationed there after the Seven Years' War.
events.significance: The act provoked widespread colonial protest under the slogan 'no taxation without representation' and helped set the stage for the American Revolution.

events.title: First Public Film Screening by the Lumière Brothers
events.description: Auguste and Louis Lumière held a private screening of their film 'La Sortie de l'usine Lumière à Lyon' (Workers Leaving the Lumière Factory) in Paris for the Society for the Encouragement of National Industry.
events.significance: This is regarded as one of the earliest demonstrations of projected motion pictures, marking the birth of cinema as a medium.

events.title: Arab League Founded in Cairo
events.description: Representatives of Egypt, Iraq, Transjordan, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, Syria and later Yemen signed the Arab League Pact in Cairo, creating a regional organization to promote cooperation among Arab states.
events.significance: The Arab League became a major forum for Arab political, economic and cultural coordination and has played a central role in Middle Eastern diplomacy.

events.title: Intel Ships the Pentium Processor
events.description: Intel began shipping its first Pentium microprocessors, the fifth generation of its x86 line, offering a large leap in performance over the 486.
events.significance: The Pentium helped bring powerful computing to the mass market and cemented Intel's dominance in the personal computer industry during the 1990s.
